business_question: Given a fixed tabular dataset, how much does automated model search actually buy over a sensible default -- and how much of the apparent gain is the search fitting its own validation folds?
success_criteria: Report the CV-to-hold-out gap for every family, not just the best score.
Any ensemble gain must be demonstrated on out-of-fold predictions only.
Quantify what a single interpretable tree gives up against the ensemble.
Audit disparity across sex, race and age band.

phases.title: 1. Business Understanding
phases.purpose: Translate a business question into a measurable data-mining goal and fix the success criteria before seeing any results.
phases.summary: The subject of this project is model selection itself, so the deliverable is a *diagnosis*, not just a leaderboard. The three questions fixed up front were: does search overfit, does stacking genuinely help, and would a simple tree have been enough?
activities: Framed the goal as measuring the value of search, not maximising a number.
Chose ROC-AUC for stability across folds, with PR-AUC reported alongside.
Declared sex, race and age band as audit-only.
Committed to distillation as a test of necessity.

findings.statement: A leaderboard without a hold-out gap is not evidence
findings.evidence: CV scores rise with every trial by construction
findings.implication: Both numbers are reported for every family.

decisions.decision: Report CV and hold-out side by side for every family.
decisions.rationale: The gap is the cost of searching and is the actual finding of an AutoML exercise.

phases.title: 2. Data Understanding
phases.purpose: Acquire the data, describe it honestly, and surface quality problems early enough that they can change the plan.
phases.summary: 48,842 census records, 23.9% above the $50k threshold, 6,465 missing cells across three columns.
activities: Profiled all features and the three sensitive attributes.
Measured the base rate within every demographic group.
Identified redundant and design-artefact columns.

findings.statement: fnlwgt is a survey design artefact
findings.evidence: Census sampling weight -- a survey-design artefact describing how many people the row represents, not a proper
findings.implication: Dropped: it describes the sampling frame, not the person, and trees find spurious structure in it.

findings.statement: education and education_num are the same variable
findings.implication: Kept the ordinal; keeping both would split one signal across two columns.

findings.statement: Base rates differ sharply across demographic groups
findings.implication: Guarantees that demographic parity and calibration cannot both hold -- the trade-off is structural, not a modelling failure.

decisions.decision: Drop fnlwgt despite its predictive correlation.
decisions.rationale: Predictive power sourced from survey design does not transfer to any deployment.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Keep it because it improves CV score
decisions.rejection_reason: Optimising a metric using an artefact is the definition of reward hacking.

phases.title: 3. Data Preparation
phases.purpose: Construct the modelling dataset: selection, cleaning, feature engineering and the train/test protocol that makes evaluation trustworthy.
phases.summary: 13 features. Rare native-country levels grouped at a 1% floor; imputation and encoding fitted per fold.
activities: Engineered capital-net, capital-gain indicator and hours bands.
Grouped categorical levels below 1% frequency.
Stratified the split on the target.

findings.statement: native_country has 42 levels, most extremely rare
findings.implication: A level seen a handful of times is a memorisation hook, not a signal.

decisions.decision: Group rare categories inside the pipeline.
decisions.rationale: The frequency table must be learned per fold.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Group them on the full dataset first
decisions.rejection_reason: The grouping decision would then be informed by the test rows.

criteria: All fitted transforms inside the Pipeline

phases.title: 4. Modeling
phases.purpose: Select techniques, search their hyperparameters, and record what was tried -- including what failed.
phases.summary: 101 hill-climbing trials over 6 families, then out-of-fold stacking and Caruana greedy selection. Caruana greedy ensemble was deployed.
activities: Hill-climbed every family on cross-validated ROC-AUC.
Scored each family once on the hold-out and recorded the gap.
Generated out-of-fold predictions for both ensembling methods.
Fitted a logistic meta-learner and a Caruana greedy blend.
Distilled the result into a depth-4 tree.

findings.statement: No family overfitted the search at this data size
findings.implication: The gap is reported per family so nobody quotes the CV number as deployed performance. Here it happens to be negative, which is a result of the measurement rather than an assumption that search is safe.

A difference in the fourth decimal place is indistinguishable from noise on a 9,769-row hold-out. The honest reading is that ensembling bought nothing here, which is what a 0.92 correlation between base learners predicts.

findings.statement: Base models agree closely with each other
findings.implication: Ensembling can only exploit disagreement; near-identical members leave nothing to combine.

decisions.decision: Train the meta-learner strictly on out-of-fold predictions.
decisions.rationale: The meta-learner is trained exclusively on out-of-fold predictions: every base-model probability it sees was produced by a model that did not train on
decisions.alternative_rejected: Fit base models on all training data, then predict that same data for the meta-learner
decisions.rejection_reason: The meta-learner then sees the labels through base-model memorisation; the gain is fictional.

decisions.decision: Report greedy selection and logistic stacking together.
decisions.rationale: Greedy cannot use negative weights; logistic can, but can overfit the OOF matrix. Neither dominates.
decisions.rejection_reason: Selecting the winner post hoc on the hold-out is itself a form of hold-out contamination.

criteria: Stacking built on out-of-fold predictions only

phases.title: 5. Evaluation
phases.purpose: Assess results against the business criteria from phase 1, not just the loss function, and review the whole process for defects.
phases.summary: Hold-out ROC-AUC 0.9314 (PR-AUC 0.8363) against 0.7543 for an analyst heuristic. A depth-4 tree reproduces 92.5% of the ensemble's decisions and 93.1% of its AUC. The gap is large enough to justify the
activities: Scored the untouched hold-out once.
Compared the ensemble against a distilled depth-4 tree.
Audited disparity on three attributes and four criteria.
Cross-checked permutation against impurity importance.

findings.statement: A depth-4 tree recovers most of the ensemble
findings.implication: he ensemble's decisions and 93.1% of its AUC. The gap is large enough to justify the ensemble where accuracy genuinely matters more than transparency.
Excluding sex and race from the features did not remove the disparity, because correlated proxies remain. This is the central lesson of the fairness literature, reproduced here.

decisions.rationale: It is the honest answer to 'was the AutoML worth it?'
decisions.rejection_reason: Implies complexity was necessary without testing it.

criteria: Fairness audited on all declared attributes

phases.title: 6. Deployment
phases.purpose: Ship the model behind an interface, with monitoring, documented limits, and a plan for the day the data drifts.
phases.summary: Both the champion pipeline and the distilled tree are pickled, so a deployment can choose accuracy or auditability explicitly rather than by default.
activities: Pickled the champion and the distilled student.
Exposed the tree's rules as readable text.
Documented the fairness findings in the model card.

findings.statement: Shipping two models makes the trade-off explicit
findings.evidence: champion and depth-4 student both served
findings.implication: A regulated context can take the auditable one and know exactly what it costs.

findings.statement: 1994 census data must not drive present-day decisions
findings.evidence: stated prominently in the model card
findings.implication: This is a methodology benchmark, not an income model.

decisions.decision: Publish the distilled tree's rules in full.
decisions.rationale: Four levels of if-statements can be read and contested by a non-specialist.
decisions.rejection_reason: Removes any possibility of external scrutiny.

iteration_notes: The first run kept fnlwgt and scored noticeably higher. The audit flagged it as a sampling artefact, and removing it cost real AUC -- which is the point: the lost performance was never available in deployment.

Stacking initially showed a large gain because the meta-learner was trained on in-fold base predictions. Rebuilding it on out-of-fold predictions shrank the gain to near zero, which is the honest number.
methodology: CRISP-DM (Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining), Chapman et al. 2000. Phases are iterative; the notes below record where this project looped back rather than proceeding linearly.
